Since January 1, 2014, Macon and Bibb County have operated as one consolidated government, and little Payne joined in 2015. An owner therefore deals with a single local government, a single county school district and a single tax commissioner.

Find the Tax Commissioner at 188 Third Street, Macon, Georgia 31201, any weekday from eight to five. Call (478) 621-6500 or write to taxinfo@maconbibb.us. This office mails the statements, prepares the yearly tax digest for the state, and splits what it collects among the State of Georgia, the county government and the school board. Your value is set elsewhere, by the Board of Tax Assessors at (478) 621-6701.

  • Tax Commissioner: statements, payments, liens, tax sales, excess funds claims
  • Tax Assessors: values, returns, homestead applications, appeal filings
  • Solid Waste Department: the garbage fee that rides along with the property bill

About 157,556 people lived in Bibb as of July 2025, barely above the 157,346 counted in 2020. Owners and renters are nearly even. The 2020 count showed exactly 50 percent each, and the newer survey puts owners at 51.4 percent. Where a house is rented, the bill still goes to whoever held title on January 1, never to the tenant.

Housing stands at 72,122 units in 2025 across 59,921 households. A typical owned home is worth $174,500, a typical rent is $1,066 a month and typical household income is $51,234. If you own a rental, expect investors to be your likeliest buyers, and a tenant's lease will shape how fast the house can close.

Statements for real and personal property go out by mid-September, with the bill divided into two installments. The first falls on October 15 and the second on November 15. If either date is a weekend, payment is due the next business day.

The owner of record on January 1 gets the first bill. A transfer reported within the 90 days before a due date is verified, and then the new owner is billed. Lenders receive a data file of amounts due, but the paper statement is mailed to the owner, who stays responsible for any missed payment even with escrow.

Mobile homes keep a schedule of their own: statements out by January 30, payment due April 1, and a decal handed out once the tax is paid. If a mobile home account is late, the state penalty applies, which is 10 percent of the tax or $5 if that is more, plus monthly interest.

• You may pay part now, though interest and penalties keep running on the remainder
  • Mail counts as on time only with a USPS date stamp
  • After a levy begins, pay a delinquent account in person

The commissioner will take any number of partial payments, but the part left unpaid keeps adding penalties and interest. Do not rely on a postage meter date for mailing proof. For delinquent accounts the office wants payment brought in by hand, above all after a levy and sale notice begin.

Ahead of a FiFa lien, a notice of intent goes to the owner, who has 30 days to pay in full. The lien is then entered on the General Execution Docket held by the Clerk of Superior Court, which can happen once a balance is open past 90 days. Pay the tax with fees, penalties and interest and the lien is cancelled. The counter never sells liens, and the office says it does not report to credit bureaus.

Every residential premises, occupied or vacant, also gets a quarterly garbage bill from the Solid Waste Department. It is a different charge from the property tax, and an appeal of your value does not pause it. A low-income household may request an exemption, filed with the Solid Waste Department by 5 p.m. each November 1.

At closing, ask the title company whether any garbage charge is still open for the quarter. It rides on the premises, so an unpaid quarterly bill can show up on a payoff request even though it has nothing to do with the property tax.

Homestead approvals come from the Tax Assessors. To qualify you own and live in the home on January 1, and an application in by April 1 covers the current year. Approval does not need annual renewal, but a move or a new deed means applying again.

State law and local acts set the amounts, so read the figure on your bill. Call the assessors at (478) 621-6701 to learn what your account carries and whether any senior relief fits. After closing, the buyer must file their own application, so mention it to their agent. If you moved out and keep the house as a rental, you no longer qualify and should say so.

Write your appeal, say which appeal method you want, and get it to the Board of Tax Assessors within 45 days of the notice. You can argue taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption. Because the Tax Commissioner is an independently elected office that neither supervises nor answers to the assessors, take appeal questions to the assessors.

A mobile home has a later cutoff, 45 days after the bill is mailed or April 1, whichever is last. You can also claim back tax collected in error or unlawfully, within three years after you paid.

With a FiFa on file, the county may levy on the parcel and sell it. Auctions take place on the courthouse steps, 206 7th Street, at 11 a.m. on the first Tuesday of any month with a sale scheduled. Bidders must show up personally. Bidding starts at the amount of tax, penalties and fees owed. The winner receives a sheriff's tax deed instead of the land, and payment, in cash, certified funds or a money order, is due within two hours.

A right of redemption survives the sale. For one year after it, the owner or any interested party can repurchase the tax deed by paying the winning bid, taxes the buyer covered later, special assessments and a 20 percent premium. Only after that year can the buyer begin foreclosing the right, using certified mail and newspaper notice for four straight weeks. A bid above the debt leaves excess funds in the office's hands, and lienholders are paid ahead of the record owner.

Pay the tax from your sale proceeds ahead of any levy, and the house never goes through that process. Request a written payoff, hand it to the closing agent and save the receipt. A buyer paying cash for the house as it stands may close fast enough to beat a sale date, and you would skip lender delays and repair requests. Need a deed copy? The Clerk of Superior Court deed room is at 601 Mulberry Street, Macon, GA 31201.

faqs.q: When must Macon-Bibb property tax be paid?
faqs.a: Two installments: October 15 and November 15. Statements go out by September 15. Dates on a weekend move to the next business day.

faqs.q: Does Macon-Bibb accept partial tax payments?
faqs.a: Yes, as many as you like. Whatever you still owe keeps drawing interest and penalties, and it may end up liened.

faqs.q: What is the appeal deadline for a Macon-Bibb assessment?
faqs.a: Send it in writing to the Board of Tax Assessors within 45 days of the notice date. The assessors' number is (478) 621-6701.

faqs.q: Where do I get a copy of my Bibb County deed?
faqs.a: Go to the deed room of the Clerk of Superior Court at 601 Mulberry Street, Macon, GA 31201, where warranty deeds are kept.

faqs.q: Does a postmark prove I paid on time in Macon-Bibb?
faqs.a: A USPS postmark does. A postage meter date does not count.
